title: Herzog hands Eisenkot mandate to form Israel's next government
h1: Israel's president gives Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, the first chance to form a government
description: President Isaac Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate on November 8, 2026 after 67 lawmakers backed him. He has 28 days, plus up to 14 more, to reach 61 seats.
standfirst: Eisenkot won more recommendations than Netanyahu, but his own bloc is well short of a majority. He is calling for a national emergency government, and Netanyahu stays prime minister until a new one is sworn in.
keywords: Eisenkot mandate form government, Israel coalition talks November 2026, Herzog Eisenkot, Netanyahu, Israel election 2026 results
takeaways: Herzog handed Eisenkot the mandate at the President's Residence on November 8, 2026, after 67 lawmakers recommended him and 46 backed Netanyahu.
Eisenkot's alliance holds 48 seats; Netanyahu's bloc holds 53; 61 of 120 are needed.
Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by up to 14, to form a government.
body: Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form the country's next government at a ceremony at the President's Residence on Sunday, November 8, The Jerusalem Post reported. Herzog chose Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff, after 67 members of the Knesset recommended him and 46 recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The numbers are difficult. The October 27 election left Eisenkot's four-party alliance with 48 seats and Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc with 53, while Arab-led parties won a record 19, Al Jazeera reported. A government needs 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats. The two Arab-led lists, Ra'am and the Joint List, recommended Eisenkot, but that does not commit them to joining him, and Eisenkot has ruled out governing with them. Al Jazeera said bringing in the ultra-Orthodox parties United Torah Judaism and Shas would give him exactly 61; United Torah Judaism did not recommend any candidate.

At the ceremony, Eisenkot repeated his call for a national emergency government and said "creative and unconventional political steps will be required," according to The Jerusalem Post. He invited every party to accept four principles he has set as conditions for joining. Herzog urged him to build a government that serves the entire public.

Eisenkot has 28 days to form a government, and Herzog can extend that by up to 14 days. If he fails, the president can give another lawmaker 28 days with no extension, and if that also fails, a majority of lawmakers can back a candidate for a final 14-day attempt before new elections, The Jerusalem Post reported. Netanyahu remains prime minister in the meantime. He has warned that a government backed by Arab-led parties "will dismantle the state of Israel from within," Al Jazeera reported.
